subtitle.en: What El Niño and La Niña mean for your county's rains, harvests, pastures, prices and food security — and what the coming season is likely to bring.

intro.en: Kenya's rains are steered from the ocean. Pick your county to see what a season puts at stake, what past El Niño and La Niña years did to its rains, pastures, prices and hunger — and what the coming season is likely to bring.

title.en: 1. What's At Stake In My County?

intro.en: *Click your county on the map (or use the dropdown above). This first section shows what its farms and herds are worth, what it grows, and who a bad season puts at risk.*

mapTitle.en: Pick a county — Kenya at a glance

mapIntro.en: *Click any county to make it the focus of every chart on this page. Recolour the map to browse counties by agricultural value, current vegetation, food insecurity or seasonal rainfall.*

mapCaption.en: Counties shaded by the chosen metric. Agricultural value is the Atlas exposure snapshot (MapSPAM 2020 crops + GLW4 livestock, constant international dollars); vegetation and food insecurity are the latest available readings; rainfall is the long-term seasonal mean. Click a county to select it; hover for its value.

mapAbout.en:
Value of production comes from the Atlas exposure layer: MapSPAM 2020 crop production and Gridded Livestock of the World 4 herd sizes, valued in constant international dollars so counties are comparable. Vegetation is the most recent 10-day NDVI reading as a percentage of its long-term normal (WFP VAM / MODIS). Food insecurity is the latest IPC phase classification for the county's worst area (FEWS NET). Rainfall means use CHIRPS v3, 1991–2020.

**Data:** IFPRI MapSPAM + FAO GLW4 · WFP VAM · FEWS NET IPC · UCSB CHC CHIRPS v3. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

vopIntro.en: *The economic stakes: the value of what this county produces, crops (green) and livestock (brown), in constant international dollars so counties are comparable. In the arid and semi-arid north and east this is overwhelmingly livestock — which is why a drought that fails pasture hits those counties hardest.*

vopCaption.en: Gross value of agricultural production by commodity (MapSPAM 2020 crops + GLW4 livestock, constant international dollars — a 2020 snapshot). What a bad season puts at economic risk here.

vopAbout.en:
Value of production (VoP) is the Atlas's standard exposure measure: physical production × international commodity prices, expressed in constant 2015 international dollars (purchasing-power comparable). Crops are from IFPRI's MapSPAM 2020 disaggregation; livestock from FAO's Gridded Livestock of the World 4. It is a snapshot of exposure, not a time series.

**Data:** IFPRI (MapSPAM) & FAO (GLW4), via the Atlas exposure layer. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

produceIntro.en: *Official county figures from the **KNBS National Agriculture Production Report**: 31 crops (2019–2024), 13 livestock species (2021–2023) and 11 livestock products (2021–2022). Blank means **not reported — never zero**.*

produceCaption.en: What the county grows and herds, from Kenya's official county returns (KNBS National Agriculture Production Report, both current editions; rice added from AFA — the one crop the KNBS county tables omit). Blanks are county-years KNBS did not report — not zero.

produceAbout.en:
**How KNBS compiles this data — and what a blank means.** Kenya's crop and livestock figures are administrative data, not a sample survey: county field extension officers estimate area, production and value per season, aggregated ward → sub-county → county; state corporations supply the value-chain crops. KNBS reconciles these returns into the annual National Agriculture Production Report. Because the source is administrative expert-estimate, coverage has gaps: **a blank county-year means KNBS did not report it — it does not mean zero production.** We leave such cells empty rather than impute 0.

**How we extracted it.** Every number was parsed from the report PDFs by a deterministic engine — no value was read or typed by a language model. Extraction is orientation-aware (landscape annexes are de-rotated by word position) and column-binned by coordinate so a blank stays blank. The primary validation is **additivity**: each crop's county figures must reconcile to the report's own printed national total; each table also passes a completeness check, and on ~90% of tables two independent PDF engines agree cell-by-cell. Tables that fail are held back, not served. For the food crops present in both editions, 2020–2024 use the latest (2024–25) edition — it folds in KNBS's prior-year revisions — and 2019 the previous one; **2024 is provisional**. Livestock annexes print no national total, so they are validated by dual-engine agreement plus cross-year plausibility. The full per-table source list is below; the validation log ships with the repository.

**Data:** KNBS National Agriculture Production Report (2023–24 + 2024–25 editions); rice from the Agriculture & Food Authority. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

produceNote.en: **Blank means not reported — never zero.** Coverage varies by crop, county and year; missing county-years are marked ∅ on the charts.

gesiTitle.en: who a bad season puts at risk

gesiIntro.en: *A few indicators where this county stands out from the national picture, from the KNBS County Gender Data Sheets. Existing hardship concentrates the impact of a failed season. The full 35-indicator table is in the [technical annex](#annex-gesi).*

gesiCaption.en: Indicators where the county sits near the top or bottom of the 47-county range (KNBS County Gender Data Sheets, 2025). Which direction is "better" varies by indicator — these mark where the county stands out, not a score.

gesiAbout.en:
Each value was read from the county's official gender data sheet by a deterministic, code-keyed parser and passed a 47-county consensus gate (the national benchmark printed on every sheet must be identical across all 47 — the extraction's built-in proof). Indicator labels are served exactly as extracted. The full table, with every county's distribution, is in the technical annex.

**Data:** KNBS County Gender Data Sheets (2025). [Methods & sources →](#methods)

title.en: 2. How Does The Ocean Steer My County's Rains?

intro.en: *Kenya has two rainy seasons, and the ocean steers each differently. The **short rains (Oct–Dec)** follow El Niño / La Niña and the **Indian Ocean Dipole** — a warm-or-cool seesaw in the Indian Ocean that moves together with ENSO and carries much of the signal. The **long rains (Mar–May)** answer mostly to a separate Pacific pattern called the **Western-V**, which moves largely on its own — El Niño tells you little about the long rains. Below, each year's season is coloured by whether it was wetter or drier than normal, with the ocean state shown underneath.*

rainTitle.en: season by season — wetter or drier than normal

rainCaption.en: Each bar is one year's season for the county: teal = wetter than the 1991–2020 normal, brown = drier. The strips underneath show the ocean state that season — El Niño / La Niña, and the Indian Ocean Dipole for the short rains; the Western-V for the long rains. Named years mark the events Kenyans remember.

rainAbout.en:
Rainfall is CHIRPS v3, aggregated to the county. The anomaly view (default) plots each season's departure from the county's own 1991–2020 mean; toggle to absolute mm, a drought index (SPEI-3, a standardised measure of how unusually dry or wet the season was, accounting for temperature), or temperature. Phase strips: El Niño/La Niña from the Niño 3.4 index averaged over the season's months (±0.5 °C threshold); IOD positive/negative from the DMI (±0.4); Western-V high/low from its standardised MAM index (±0.5). One caution: the climate baseline itself is shifting — the long rains have declined over recent decades — so "normal" is a moving target.

**Data:** CHIRPS v3 rainfall + CHIRTS temperature + SPEI (UCSB Climate Hazards Center, via the Atlas hub); drivers NOAA CPC / HadISST. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

phaseChipsNote.en: Season averages by ocean state (computed live from the data above):

calendarTitle.en: when does my county plant and harvest?

calendarIntro.en: *The crop calendar links the ocean signal to the field: planting follows the rains, harvest comes months later — so a failed season shows up in food and markets with a lag.*

calendarCaption.en: Planting (light) and harvest (dark) windows per crop and season (JRC ASAP crop calendar), against the short-rains and long-rains windows. Covers 38 of 47 counties.

calendarNoData.en: *No rainfed crop calendar exists for this county — it is a pastoralist (arid/semi-arid) or urban county with no main cropping season. Its seasonality is the rains themselves and pasture greenness — see the vegetation chart in [section 3](#events), which covers all 47 counties. Crop-calendar coverage: 38 of 47 counties.*

contingencyTitle.en: how often did each ocean state bring wet or dry seasons here?

contingencyIntro.en: *The county's own record, counted season by season: for each ocean state, how many past seasons ended wetter, near-normal, or drier than usual. With no ocean signal each third would be equally likely — the dashed line.*

contingencyCaption.en: Counts of the county's past seasons (1981–2025) by outcome tercile — wetter / near-normal / drier than the 1991–2020 normal — grouped by the ocean state in that season: El Niño / Neutral / La Niña for the short rains; Western-V high / neutral / low for the long rains. The dashed line marks the one-third share expected by chance. Counts, not a forecast.

mapsComing.en: *🗺️ A season-by-season **rainfall map explorer** (county and subcounty CHIRPS v3 maps through time) is being developed separately and will slot in here.*

can.en: **This section can tell you:** which ocean states have historically leaned your county's seasons wetter or drier, and how consistently.

cannot.en: **It cannot tell you:** what any single coming season will do — an ocean state shifts the odds; it never guarantees an outcome.

annexPointer.en: → *How strong are these links statistically — correlations, driver mechanics, uncertainty? See the [technical annex](#annex-drivers).*

title.en: 3. What Did Past El Niño And La Niña Years Do Here?

intro.en: *The events Kenyans remember — the 1997–98 El Niño floods, the 2010–11 and 2016–17 droughts, the 2020–23 triple-dip La Niña, the 2023 El Niño — traced through this county's pastures, food security, markets and harvests. The shaded bands mark those events on every chart.*

timelineCaption.en: Named climate events referenced throughout this section. Hover for the one-line story; the same shading appears on every chart below.

ndviTitle.en: pasture and vegetation through the events

ndviIntro.en: *The clearest bridge from a failed season to people — especially in pastoralist counties, where livelihoods ride on pasture. The line is 10-day vegetation greenness (NDVI) as a percentage of its normal: below 100 (orange) = drought stress; above (green) = greener than usual.*

ndviCaption.en: Ten-day NDVI as a percentage of that period's long-term normal (MODIS via WFP VAM, aggregated to the county, 2002–present). Orange = vegetation deficit; green = greener than normal. Event bands as above.

ndviPhaseTitle.en: short-rains greenness, year by year, grouped by ocean state

ndviPhaseCaption.en: Each dot is one year's short-rains (Oct–Dec) mean vegetation for the county, as % of normal, grouped by that season's ENSO state (2002–present). A dot's label is its year. This is the county-level climate-impact record the short production series cannot yet provide.

ipcCaption.en: IPC food-insecurity phase for the county's worst area (FEWS NET, Current Situation). Phase 3 is **Crisis**, phase 4 **Emergency**; the phase holds until reclassified (steps, not slopes). Event bands as above.

pricesIntro.en: *Monthly retail prices in the county's monitored markets (FEWS NET). Raw prices mix inflation with scarcity — switch to the **change vs a year earlier** or **seasonal anomaly** view to see the climate signal.*

pricesCaption.en: Monthly retail price by market for the selected product. Dots are actual observations; lines break across gaps longer than ~3 months. The anomaly views are computed from the same series: % change vs the same month a year earlier, or the departure from that market's usual level for that calendar month.

pricesAbout.en:
Retail-only series from FEWS NET's price database, so the unit stays consistent within a product. Nominal Kenyan shillings over long periods mostly show inflation — the two anomaly views isolate the unusual part: **vs year earlier** is the 12-month percent change; **seasonal anomaly** compares each month to that market's typical level for that calendar month (in standard deviations). Both are computed directly from the plotted series.

**Data:** FEWS NET (FDW retail market prices). [Methods & sources →](#methods)

pricesNoData.en: *No FEWS NET market price series is available for this county (coverage: 42 of 47 counties).*

totTitle.en: the pastoral squeeze — what a goat buys

totIntro.en: *The classic drought signal in pastoral economies: how many kilograms of maize one goat buys. In a drought, herders sell weakened animals cheap exactly when cereal prices spike — the ratio collapses.*

totCaption.en: Terms of trade: the county's median goat price divided by its median maize price (kg), month by month — kilograms of maize one goat buys. Computed from the two FEWS NET retail series. Event bands as above.

totNoData.en: *No goat price series is monitored in this county (goat prices cover ~20 of 47 counties) — the terms-of-trade view needs both a goat and a maize series.*

prodIntro.en: *The county production record is short — six years — but it happens to span Kenya's longest drought in decades (2020–23 La Niña) and the 2023–24 El Niño recovery. Six years is far too short for statistics, so read this as event history: what happened, not a rule.*

prodCaption.en: Production of the county's main crops, 2019–2024 (KNBS NAPR; rice from AFA), with the season's ocean state underneath and the named events shaded. ∅ marks county-years KNBS did not report — **not zero**. Six data points allow no correlation claims; this is an aligned history.

rwIntro.en: *County-tagged humanitarian and disaster reports (ReliefWeb, 2010–present). Report volume reflects attention as well as severity — a context layer, not an impact measure.*

rwCaption.en: County-tagged reports per year, stacked by first-matching hazard (drought → flood → epidemic → other). Event bands as above. The most recent reports are listed in the expander below.

can.en: **This section can tell you:** how the named ocean events played out in this county — pasture, food security, prices, harvests — as recorded history.

cannot.en: **It cannot tell you:** that ENSO *caused* each impact by itself (conflict, prices and hunger have many drivers), nor anything statistical about six years of county harvests.

annexPointer.en: → *Conflict data, the national production–climate statistics, and the full trade detail are in the [technical annex](#annex).*

title.en: 4. What Is The Coming Season Likely To Bring?

intro.en: *What the ocean is doing now, and what that state has historically meant for this county's next season. History-based guidance — not a rainfall forecast; the official Kenyan forecast is the Kenya Meteorological Department's.*

recentTitle.en: the three ocean signals, recent years

recentCaption.en: Each signal on its own scale: Niño 3.4 (°C, El Niño above the dashed threshold, La Niña below), the Indian Ocean Dipole (DMI), and the Western-V (standardised). The shaded band marks each signal's neutral zone.

recentAbout.en:
Niño 3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly from NOAA CPC; DMI from HadISST (coalesced with ERSST to reach the present); Western-V computed from ERSSTv5 following Funk et al. 2018 (validated against the published series). The three are plotted on separate scales because their units differ — a shared axis would misleadingly make the standardised Western-V look permanently extreme.

**Data:** NOAA CPC · NOAA PSL / Met Office Hadley Centre · derived Western-V. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

ondIntro.en: *The official ENSO-state forecast (NOAA CPC) says which phase is coming. History says what that phase has meant here: the map colours every county by what its short rains **usually did** in the past seasons most like the one forecast. An analogue of similar past years — **not a rainfall forecast**.*

outlookMapNote.en: Strong colour = most similar years mostly agreed; pale = they leaned that way but disagreed more. Hover any county for its counts. The selected county is outlined.

outlookCaption.en: Each county's most common short-rains outcome (wetter / near-normal / drier than the 1991–2020 normal) across the analogue years — the past ENSO seasons most similar to the current forecast state. Colour strength encodes how consistently the analogues agreed. An analogue composite, not a forecast.

outlookAbout.en:
Analogue years are past October–December seasons whose ENSO state (relative Niño index) matched the forecast phase, ranked by similarity to the current index value — nearest neighbours, not strongest events. Each county is coloured by its most common rainfall tercile across those years, saturated where the agreement is strong and pale where it is weak; counties with no baseline are hatched. With eight analogue seasons, chance alone would give roughly a third to each outcome — shares near one-third mean little.

**Data:** CHIRPS v3 county rainfall + NOAA CPC ENSO-state probabilities and relative Niño index. [Methods & sources →](#methods)

offDiagonalWarn.en: ⚠️ **The two short-rains signals currently disagree.** ENSO and the Indian Ocean Dipole usually move together in Oct–Dec — right now they do not, and in past seasons like this the ENSO-only reading was least reliable. Treat the map and verdict below with extra caution; the IOD-based reading is shown alongside for comparison.

mamTitle.en: long rains (Mar–May) — history only, no outlook

mamIntro.en: *The long rains cannot be skilfully forecast from ENSO — they answer mostly to the Western-V, which has no official forecast. So for Mar–May we show **history only**: how this county's long rains behaved in past Western-V states. No skilful long-rains outlook exists in this notebook; the Kenya Meteorological Department's seasonal forecast is the place to look.*

mamCaption.en: The county's past long-rains outcomes grouped by the Western-V state in those years (1981–2025) — a historical relationship, explicitly **not an outlook**. The dashed line is the one-third share expected by chance.

watch.en: **What to watch, and where.** The official Kenyan seasonal forecast and weather warnings are the **Kenya Meteorological Department**'s: [seasonal outlook](https://meteo.go.ke/forecast/seasonal-forecast) and [current warnings](https://meteo.go.ke/warnings) (meteo.go.ke). For the global ENSO state itself, the [NOAA CPC ENSO advisory](https://www.cpc.ncep.noaa.gov/products/analysis_monitoring/enso_advisory/ensodisc.shtml) updates monthly. The short rains are the forecastable season (the IOD gives usable lead time); the long rains are not — treat any Mar–May guidance as low-confidence.

can.en: **This section can tell you:** which way history leans for the coming short rains given the forecast ocean state, and how consistent that lean has been.

cannot.en: **It cannot tell you:** the actual rainfall forecast (that is KMD's), anything skilful about the long rains, or an outcome — eight similar past years shift odds, nothing more.

intro.en: *Tools rather than story: put counties side by side, and see the national trade context. Comparison defaults to the selected county and its neighbours.*

compareIntro.en: *Each line is one county; the season follows the control at the top of the page.*

rainCaption.en: Seasonal rainfall (CHIRPS v3) for each selected county. Labels sit at the line ends; the season follows the page control.

ndviCaption.en: Annual-mean NDVI as % of normal for each selected county; the dashed line at 100 is the long-term normal.

tradeTitle.en: national context — Kenya's cross-border food trade

tradeIntro.en: *National, not county: Kenya is a structural maize importer (Uganda, Tanzania), and imports surge when seasons fail — as in the 2021–22 drought. Measured at national border points (FEWS NET); the flow map is in the [technical annex](#annex-trade).*

importsCaption.en: Imports into Kenya per year by partner country for the selected product (FEWS NET cross-border trade monitoring; informal flows are field estimates). National data — the same for every county.

intro.en: *The full technical record behind the story above: driver mechanics, the statistical strength of the teleconnections, the national production analysis, conflict data, the complete GESI table, trade detail, and per-dataset methods. Written for analysts.*

a1Intro.en: *The ocean indices themselves and how they interact. ENSO and the IOD are one coupled Indo-Pacific system in the short rains; the Western-V is a partly-separate control on the long rains (Niño 3.4 ↔ Western-V correlation ≈ 0 — computed live below).*

driverTitle.en: the selected index, season by season

driverCaption.en: The selected ocean index as a per-year seasonal mean; points coloured by ENSO phase. The Western-V index is defined and standardised for Mar–May — other windows are shown for context only.

interactCaption.en: Each point is one Oct–Dec season: ENSO (Niño 3.4) against the IOD (DMI), coloured by the IOD's sign that year, with the fitted line and live correlation in the heading. The two behave as one coupled system in the short rains.

combinedCaption.en: All three drivers standardised against 1991–2020 so they share one axis. Read as the ocean regime: all positive = strong wet signal for the short rains; ENSO/IOD negative = drought risk.

a2Title.en: A2 · How strong are the links, really?

a2Intro.en: *The statistical evidence behind section 2, computed live in the browser from the served data. Correlations use the full 1981–2025 county record; production comparisons acknowledge their six-year limit.*

corrTitle.en: county correlation map — seasonal rainfall vs driver

corrCaption.en: Pearson correlation between each county's seasonal rainfall anomaly and the driver index for that season, 1981–2025. Counties where the correlation is not significant (p > 0.05) are greyed. With 47 counties tested at once, a few would pass by chance — treat the spatial pattern, not any single county, as the finding (no multiple-testing correction applied).

dotTitle.en: county harvests vs season rainfall — six years, a pattern check

dotCaption.en: Each labelled dot is one year (2019–2024): the growing-season rainfall percentile (vs the county's 1981–2025 record) against that year's production relative to the county's own median. **Six seasons — a pattern check, not a statistic.** Season windows follow the county's crop calendar where available.

a3Title.en: A3 · National production vs drivers (the honest statistics)

a3Intro.en: *Kenya has no long county production series yet, so the statistical production–climate test uses **national FAOSTAT**, detrended (the strong upward production trend would otherwise swamp the climate signal). The relationship is weak and mostly not significant — shown as such. National maize is long-rains dominated, so the short-rains signal is diluted here; the county-level effect awaits a longer county series. One caution: trying many crops until one looks significant is itself a statistical trap — read the ensemble of results, not the best one.*

scatterCaption.en: National detrended production anomaly against the season-window driver; live correlation, sample size and significance in the heading. The regression line is dashed and faint when not significant — a weak relationship is not dressed up as a signal.

trendCaption.en: The raw national production series and its fitted linear trend — what is subtracted to form the detrended anomaly above (FAOSTAT, 1961–present).

a5Title.en: A5 · County detail: GESI, conflict, trade flows

gesiFullTitle.en: all GESI indicators — county vs Kenya

gesiFullCaption.en: Every served indicator from the county's KNBS Gender Data Sheet against the 47-county distribution (grey dots), the national value (◇) and the county median (│). Rank is by raw value — which direction is "better" varies by indicator. Labels appear exactly as extracted from the sheets.

acledIntro.en: *Conflict fatalities recorded for the county (ACLED). Kept in the annex deliberately: conflict has many drivers, and the climate–conflict association in this data is **suggestive only** (a permutation test does not reach significance) — it must never be read as a county ranking or a causal claim.*

acledCaption.en: Conflict fatalities per year recorded for the county (ACLED). Context for the impacts pathway; the climate–conflict link is exploratory and not statistically established.

tradeMapCaption.en: Total recorded flows by partner for the selected product (FEWS NET XBT, 2010–2024). Arrow width is scaled by quantity (legend below); arrows connect country centres, not actual crossings. National border-point data.

intro.en: *Every dataset behind this page, how it was processed, and how to verify it. The full acquisition manifest — source URLs, licences, build scripts and per-file metadata — is versioned with this notebook in [`data/KE-enso-explorer/DATA.md`](https://github.com/AdaptationAtlas/atlas_notebooks/blob/notebooks/KE-enso-explorer-dev/data/KE-enso-explorer/DATA.md).*

drivers.en: **Ocean drivers.** Niño 3.4 / ONI / RONI from NOAA CPC (validated r=0.998 against NOAA's published series); Indian Ocean Dipole (DMI) from HadISST via NOAA PSL, coalesced with ERSST to reach the present; Western-V computed from ERSSTv5 following Funk et al. 2018 (reproduces the published post-1997 long-rains sign). ENSO-state probabilities from NOAA CPC's official RONI forecast table.

rainfall.en: **Rainfall, temperature and drought index.** CHIRPS v3 precipitation, CHIRTS-ERA5 temperature and SPEI, zonally aggregated to Kenya's 47 counties (GAUL 2024 boundaries) in the Atlas data pipeline. Seasonal values are the county mean over the season window; anomalies use the 1991–2020 reference. Note the reference period sits inside a warming, drying-long-rains record — the baseline itself is not stationary.

production.en: **Production.** County crops: KNBS National Agriculture Production Report, both current editions, extracted by a deterministic engine with additivity-to-printed-total as the primary gate (details in the produce panel's About). Rice from the Agriculture & Food Authority. National staples for the statistical test: FAOSTAT, linearly detrended per crop before relating to drivers. Livestock population and products: KNBS NAPR annexes, dual-engine validated.

impacts.en: **Impacts.** IPC food-security phase (FEWS NET, worst-area Current Situation); retail market prices (FEWS NET FDW; anomaly views computed from the served series); NDVI vegetation condition (MODIS via WFP VAM, % of dekadal normal, pixel-weighted to county); humanitarian reports (UN OCHA ReliefWeb, county-tagged); conflict (ACLED, aggregated weekly county counts — annex only); cross-border trade (FEWS NET XBT, national border points).

outlook.en: **Outlook method.** The short-rains analogue outlook picks past OND seasons whose ENSO state matches the CPC forecast phase, nearest-neighbour ranked by relative-Niño-index similarity (not by event strength), and reports each county's tercile outcomes across those years with agreement encoded as colour strength. It is a historical analogue, not a rainfall forecast; the official Kenyan seasonal forecast is KMD's. No long-rains outlook is offered — the long rains are not skilfully forecastable from ENSO, and the Western-V has no operational forecast.

honesty.en: **Anti-hallucination rule.** No numeric value on this page was produced by a language model reading and typing it: every number is either parsed by deterministic code with a validation gate (dual-engine / additivity / cross-edition / consensus) or computed live in the browser from the served data. Tables that fail their gate are held back, not served. Missing KNBS county-years are gaps, never zeros.

statusNeutral.en: The Pacific is in a neutral state

iodPos.en: the Indian Ocean Dipole is positive

iodNeg.en: the Indian Ocean Dipole is negative

iodNeu.en: the Indian Ocean Dipole is near neutral

mixedFlag.en: ⚠ mixed signals — see the outlook section

wetAfterDrought.en: Good for pasture recovery and planting — but after drought, heavy short rains bring flash-flood and livestock-disease risk, as in 1997 and 2023.

wet.en: Historically good for planting and pasture — but heavy seasons carry flood risk in low-lying areas.

dry.en: Plan for pasture and water stress: past seasons like this leaned dry here — early destocking and water planning beat late response.

near.en: No strong lean either way in past similar seasons — watch the KMD updates as the season approaches.

canCannotTitle.en: What this can and cannot tell you
